This cycle's own joint read of valuewarmup-klroll-acq1 (freeze+guard) and klrollctrl-acq1 (guard-only, no freeze) showed: (1) kl-rollback=0.05 ALONE (no actor-freeze needed) reaches the SAME plateau as freeze+guard, just faster (guard-only 8M checkpoint already at pos 0.068/0.082, neg -0.120/-0.118, matching freeze+guard's own 10-22M plateau of pos 0.07-0.086, neg -0.10 to -0.135) -- freeze is refuted as adding anything beyond the guard; (2) both 0.05 arms land at a genuinely NEW, ~2x-higher floor than every prior naked mechanism class (0.024-0.055) but still fall short of the >=0.10-both-signs PASS bar on the positive sign (final 0.068-0.069 pos, both clear 0.10 on neg). This is the direct dose-response test the finding motivates: identical recipe to klrollctrl-acq1 (no freeze, same turnpay-canary init, same seed) except --kl-rollback 0.05->0.02 (tighter, matching the trainer's own --target-kl=0.02 exactly). Prediction-if-true (update-size is the dominant, monotonic driver): the plateau rises further, closing more of the gap to 0.10 pos. Prediction-if-false (0.05 already captured most of the achievable gain / diminishing returns or over-tightening stalls learning entirely): plateau unchanged or authority/gait quality regresses (KL cap too tight to let the policy adapt at all).

**verdict**: ACQ PARTIAL-BETTER (own scope). Plain English: tightening the guard-only (no actor-freeze) update-size cap 0.05->0.02 makes turn authority peak MUCH higher early in training (best in the whole campaign) but does not fix the late-training erosion that guard-only already showed at 0.05 -- freeze, not cap tightness, is what buys durability. Own 19-point probe_turn_authority curve (TURNCAP_CFG_SET, built on-pod train-1, 4 rollouts/ckpt, /tmp/klrolltight_guardonly_turn_authority_all.jsons): peaks 2M-10M at pos 0.11-0.13/neg -0.13 to -0.17 (BOTH signs clear the >=0.10 PASS bar with room to spare -- the highest turn authority seen anywhere in this campaign, beating even the durable freeze+guard-0.05 arm's plateau), then declines steadily from ~12M onward through a mid-run 0.09-0.10 band down to a final-38M floor of pos 0.0754/0.0743, neg -0.1154/-0.1204. Final reads DO clear this run's own PARTIAL-BETTER bar vs both 0.05 arms (pos>0.069 [klrollctrl-acq1 0.055, valuewarmup_klroll_acq1 0.068] -- yes; neg more negative than -0.110 -- yes) but miss PASS (pos<0.10). Mechanism: train/kl_rollback_count fires 5x in the first update (approx_kl shock, same generic pattern as every sibling), 19 more scattered through 6.68M steps, then ZERO further rollbacks for the remaining 31.3M steps (guard fully satisfied) -- yet authority keeps eroding all the way to 38M despite no further oversized updates being blocked. This decouples 'guard engaging' from 'durability': the late-training decline is driven by ordinary small compliant gradient steps accumulating drift over a long window, not by unblocked large jumps -- tightening the cap only raises the early ceiling (steady-state approx_kl median 0.005-0.008 here vs the 0.05 arm's 0.01-0.03) and does not slow the erosion rate. Confound worth flagging: the freeze+guard sibling's actor only trains for 30M of the 38M budget (8M frozen), so its apparent 'durability' may partly reflect a shorter drift window rather than protection per se -- next freeze/no-freeze comparison should control total actor-update steps, not just wall-clock budget, to separate the two. In-training clean: eval/walk survived_frac=1, eval/walk_startjitter survived_frac=1 throughout (eval/raise 0.5 is the separate rise-submode GRU core, not this probe's scope), reward quarters 250.7/1357.5/1551.1/1523.4 (rising then flat, no collapse). JOINT dose-response conclusion (closes the pair with valuewarmup-klrolltight-acq1, already verdicted ACQ PARTIAL-BETTER): tightening the cap helps BOTH arms' peak, but only the freeze+guard combination converts that into a durable full-budget result: freeze+guard=0.02 final 0.080/0.076 pos, -0.113/-0.118 neg (this cycle's other verdict) beats guard-only=0.02 final 0.075/0.074 pos, -0.115/-0.120 neg on the positive sign that matters for the PASS bar. No further no-freeze-only tightening arm is warranted -- the mechanism (erosion continues after the guard stops firing) predicts a tighter cap would not rescue this branch's durability. The freeze+guard branch is already being pushed one notch tighter (valuewarmup-klrolltight2-acq1, --kl-rollback=0.01, launched previous cycle, currently training) -- that is the correct next step toward the >=0.10-both-signs PASS bar, not a repeat on this branch.
